content.value_statement: Rust error enums can become verbose and lose source context. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create idiomatic thiserror types.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Rust error enums for thiserror derive usage.
Suggests #[error] messages for unit, tuple, and struct variants.
Shows patterns for layered domain, infrastructure, and application errors.
Identifies missing source chains and vague error messages.
Provides focused guidance for Result aliases and custom error construction.
limitations: Does not compile or test Rust projects by itself.
Does not replace project-specific API design review.
Focuses on thiserror and not every Rust error-handling crate.
May need project context to choose public error variants.

use_cases.title: Refactor manual error implementations
use_cases.description: Convert hand-written Display and Error implementations into concise thiserror enums.

use_cases.title: Design library error APIs
use_cases.description: Create stable public error types with clear messages and preserved source chains.

use_cases.title: Review error propagation patterns
use_cases.description: Check whether #[from], #[source], or transparent wrappers fit each error boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Review one error enum
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small custom error type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Rust error enum and suggest a thiserror version with clear messages and correct derives.

prompt_templates.title: Improve source chains
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my error variants for missing source chains. Explain where #[from] or #[source] should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Design layered errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Design thiserror enums for my domain, infrastructure, and application layers. Explain the conversion boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit public error API
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced library API review before release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my public Rust error API for thiserror usage, stable variant names, source preservation, and actionable messages.

output_examples.input: A manual Display implementation for a small Rust error enum.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a concise thiserror derive, clearer variant messages, and removal of repetitive display boilerplate.

output_examples.input: An error variant that wraps an IO error without source metadata.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that the underlying cause should be preserved, so callers can inspect the original IO failure.

output_examples.input: A layered service with database, domain, and application failures.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes separate error enums for each layer and describes where automatic conversions should occur.

best_practices: Use actionable error messages that include useful context without exposing secrets.
Preserve underlying causes with #[from], #[source], or transparent wrappers when appropriate.
Keep public library errors stable and avoid leaking private implementation details.
anti_patterns: Using vague messages such as Error or Something went wrong.
Wrapping dependency errors without preserving the source chain.
Using #[from] when custom context must be added during construction.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design Rust error types that use thiserror clearly and preserve useful debugging context.

faq.question: Does it run cargo commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is guidance-only and its allowed tools are Read and Grep.

faq.question: When should I use #[from]?
faq.answer: Use #[from] when a variant should automatically convert from one source error type.

faq.question: When should I use #[source]?
faq.answer: Use #[source] when you need custom construction while still preserving the underlying cause.

faq.question: Can it help with library APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest stable error enums, transparent wrappers, and messages suitable for public APIs.

faq.question: Does it replace error handling design?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused thiserror guidance and still needs project context for final design choices.
